title: Individualized Internet-based cognitive behavioral therapy for patients with suicidal ideation: a pilot randomized controlled trial
summary:
Many people who experience thoughts about ending their life do not receive adequate psychological care. This may be due to feelings of shame, fear of stigma, or structural barriers within health care systems. Digital treatment approaches have the potential to reduce some of these barriers, as they can be accessed flexibly and independent of location. Although internet-based psychological treatments are increasingly available, their safety and practical use for people with suicidal thoughts have not yet been sufficiently studied.
The aim of this study is to examine the feasibility and safety of an internet-based psychological treatment that combines regular video sessions with therapists and guided online exercises. In addition, the study seeks to assess whether the planned study procedures, particularly the recruitment of participants and their allocation to treatment groups, can be implemented as intended.
In this study, participants in the experimental group will receive a psychological treatment delivered through video sessions with additional online materials lasting for six weeks. Throughout the study, possible unwanted or distressing effects are systematically monitored. Furthermore, the experiences and perspectives of both participants and therapists are collected through interviews and questionnaires to inform the design of future larger-scale studies.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- suicidal ideation (BSS-Screen > 2),
- sufficient German language skills,
- informed consent
- internet access at home
- residence within a radius of 70 kilometers from the respective outpatient clinic
Exclusion criteria:
- acute psychotic states, manic/hypomanic episode; substance use disorder
- suicide intent in need of immediate inpatient treatment (ability to take distance from suicide intent and/or ability to give agreements not given)
- cognitive impairment and
additional psychotherapeutic treatment
